characters.name: James McGill

characters.description: An imperator in hiding who relies on McGill's personal loyalty. She wants him to find Drusus and help arrange a witnessed death followed by a concealed revival, allowing her to escape the political danger surrounding her.
characters.name: Galina Turov

characters.description: A former consul whose public locator and official registry presence have vanished. McGill searches for him after Galina makes his disappearance central to her request.
characters.name: Drusus

characters.description: The senior defense official occupying the position once held by Drusus. He refuses to discuss the missing former consul remotely and instead orders McGill to report to his office.
characters.name: Wurtenberger

characters.description: A blue-scaled Saurian known to McGill from earlier conflicts. He leads the violent extraction that removes McGill from police custody and takes control of him.
characters.name: Saurian operative

characters.description: A member of Earth's ruling council who is pressing Galina toward the consulship. She believes he and the other council members would use her as a disposable political instrument.
characters.name: Galina's father

characters.description: The red-haired leader of armed followers in a Dust World cave complex. McGill presents the disguised Galina to her and manufactures an apparent threat that prompts the followers to kill Galina.
characters.name: Boudica

characters.description: McGill's daughter, now living in the Dust World cave community with Florimel and the Investigator. She is present when McGill brings Galina before Boudica.
characters.name: Etta

characters.description: A resident of the hidden Dust World cave complex where McGill takes Galina. She is part of the small group living there with Etta and the Investigator.
characters.name: Florimel

characters.description: A resident of the Dust World cave complex where McGill brings Galina. The Investigator lives there with Etta and Florimel among Boudica's armed followers.
characters.name: The Investigator

characters.description: An Earth-born Hegemony security specialist stationed on Dust World. Etta tells McGill that they are engaged and that her fiance transferred there to be near her.
characters.name: Etta's fiance

characters.description: A Legion Varus primus who supervises McGill after Winslade removes him from Third Unit. She explains why crystal gravity weapons make dense metal armor and equipment especially dangerous.
characters.name: Primus Collins

characters.description: The Legion Varus tribune overseeing the Crystal World expedition. He punishes McGill for missing muster by stripping him of Third Unit and assigning him to shipboard administrative work.
characters.name: Winslade

characters.description: A Third Unit adjunct and leader of its heavy troops. He returns to service under McGill when the centurion regains command for the shipboard combat exercise.
characters.name: Harris

characters.description: A Third Unit adjunct who remains with the formation when McGill resumes command. He enters the King of the Hill exercise as part of the badly outnumbered defending unit.
characters.name: Leeson

characters.description: A Third Unit fighter recognized as the formation's best user of primitive thrown weapons. His ability is especially valuable when the shipboard exercise limits the troops to spears and knives.
characters.name: Sargon

characters.description: The Legion Varus primus who starts and oversees the shipboard King of the Hill contest. He places Third Unit on the central hill while every other unit in its cohort enters with orders to remove it.
characters.name: Graves

characters.description: A Third Unit soldier who helps carry ammunition to the hilltop defenders during the shipboard exercise. He supports the line as the coordinated assault reaches McGill's position.
characters.name: Carlos

characters.description: A Legion Varus technical specialist serving with Third Unit. During the hill defense, she helps move ammunition to the troops holding the summit.
characters.name: Kivi

characters.description: A Legion Varus technical specialist attached to Third Unit. She supports the hilltop defense by carrying ammunition during the attackers' final coordinated charge.
characters.name: Natasha

characters.description: The commander of a rebuilt allied fleet that intercepts Scorpio after detecting a stealthy crystal force. He takes operational control and requires the human transports for the approaching battle.
characters.name: Allied fleet admiral

characters.description: An officer attending the coalition command conference on how to overcome Crystal World's surface batteries.
characters.name: Merton

characters.description: The Legion Varus primus whom McGill privately calls Cherish and with whom he once had an informal relationship. Assigned to monitor him, she insists that he use her rank and surname in public and maintain professional boundaries.
characters.name: Cherish Collins

characters.description: An alien assault-capsule pilot identified by a serial number until McGill nicknames him Seven. His superiors expect him to remain aboard an expendable capsule while it delivers the Crystal World beachhead force.
characters.name: Seven

characters.description: A Third Unit scout sent to examine the first apparently empty settlement on Crystal World. He disappears during the reconnaissance, turning the nearby inhabitants into an immediate concern.
characters.name: Cooper

characters.description: Cooper's scouting partner during the first survey of a Crystal World settlement. She reports his disappearance and withdraws under stealth when McGill orders the scouts back.
characters.name: Della

characters.description: The commander of the Saurian legion deploying through the beachhead. He delays committing troops at first, then reinforces McGill when the rock-bodied inhabitants attack.
characters.name: Saurian tribune

characters.description: A senior biological specialist asked to examine a living fragment captured from one of Crystal World's rock-bodied inhabitants. Her expertise is needed to clarify the enemy's unusual physical nature.
characters.name: Evelyn Thompson

characters.description: The lone Claver accompanying the deployed ape and dogman contingent. Calling himself X, he claims command of the entire force as it arrives to fortify the Crystal World beachhead.
characters.name: Claver X

characters.description: A Legion Varus primus serving with the command staff. He is killed with Winslade when a landmine explodes near the gateway posts.
characters.name: Primus Gilbert

characters.description: Galina Turov's father and the council power broker who sent McGill into the coalition campaign. He acknowledges ordering damage to the alliance, accepts limited responsibility for the operation's excesses, and suspends McGill's pending punishment.
characters.name: Alexander Turov

characters.description: A guest staying with McGill's family after McGill returns from the Crystal World campaign. Etta is anxious for McGill to come home while Derek is there.
characters.name: Derek

recaps.ending: The launcher explodes before it can fire on Earth, killing McGill's commando team and every coalition combatant nearby. McGill is revived, but Legion Varus is only slowly being restored. Wurtenberger, now consul, demotes Graves, orders his execution, and confines him pending a possible return to service. Winslade is alive after revival, while McGill remains unsure who truly initiated the launcher order. Seven survives through human revival and becomes an official Earth adviser on the divided Galactic powers. Alexander Turov confirms that he wanted the coalition damaged, suspends McGill's punishment, and regrets the loss of technology Earth cannot reproduce. On Dust World, the illicit facility has expanded and successfully revived Galina after Boudica killed her twice. Boudica expels both Galina and McGill, and McGill takes Galina home. She remains an imperator but must repair her political standing, while Drusus remains imprisoned and the silicoid threat is unresolved. Etta and Derek are married, and McGill accepts Derek into the family.
recaps.in_short: Galina Turov asks James McGill to stage her death so she can evade the consulship, but Boudica secretly holds her on Dust World. Alexander Turov then sends McGill and Legion Varus into a coalition campaign while privately ordering him to undermine the alliance. After an allied victory over a crystal fleet, the coalition lands on Crystal World, battles tunneling silicoids, and advances on a vast launcher. When the weapon targets Earth, McGill's commandos sabotage it and die in the explosion, which also destroys the surrounding coalition force and valuable technology. Wurtenberger punishes Graves for ordering the strike, while Alexander Turov later suspends McGill's own penalty. McGill finds Galina revived at an illicit Dust World facility and returns her to Earth, where her imperator position is uncertain. He then learns that Etta and Derek have married and accepts Derek as family.

recaps.text: Previously: James McGill serves as a centurion in Legion Varus and has longstanding personal and political ties to Imperator Galina Turov. His daughter Etta lives on Dust World with Florimel and the Investigator, whose hidden community operates beyond ordinary Earth control. McGill also knows Boudica, an armed Dust World leader, and has a history with Drusus, Wurtenberger, Winslade, Harris, Leeson, Kivi, Natasha, Sargon, and Evelyn Thompson. Earth uses revival technology to restore the dead, while purgatory can preserve a person's mind without returning the body. McGill's earlier actions left personal debts on both sides of Earth's power structure. The wider political order includes rival human, Saurian, Rigelian, Claver, and other alien interests, with old conflicts and alliances continuing to shape Legion Varus deployments.

Galina Turov summons McGill from leave and asks him to find the vanished Drusus, then help her escape pressure to become consul. McGill learns that Drusus and his staff were purged, with Drusus held as a disembodied mind in the Vault of the Forgotten. Wurtenberger authorizes an attempt to reach him, but an Intelligence officer intercepts McGill. McGill kills the officer, escapes Central, and becomes a fugitive. Galina's Saurian agents extract him to her yacht. She explains that the ruling council, including her father, would treat her as a disposable consul. Her solution is a public assassination followed by revival somewhere McGill cannot reveal. They travel covertly through Geneva to Dust World. In Boudica's cave complex, McGill exposes Galina's identity, plants a knife in her hand, and frames her as an attacker. Boudica's followers stab Galina to death, completing the staged killing while leaving her intended revival site secret.

McGill preserves Galina's revival data, but Boudica changes the arrangement. She proposes that the Investigator revive Galina off-grid and keep her hidden, using her disappearance against the council. McGill agrees to help Boudica reach Death World if Etta can leave Dust World. Etta reveals that she intends to marry her fiance, a Hegemony security specialist who transferred to be near her. The Investigator estimates that Galina's revival will take weeks. McGill and Boudica enter Geneva in disguise, but Galina's father's Saurian operative recognizes them. Boudica is allowed to continue toward Death World while McGill is detained and interrogated about Galina. Her father stops the interrogation, then confronts McGill directly. He sends McGill back to Legion Varus for a joint strike against a crystal base. In private, he also orders McGill to sabotage the coalition afterward, blame Rigel, and restart the conflict with the Rigelians. Failure means confinement beside Drusus in the Vault of the Forgotten.

McGill reaches Scorpio after missing muster. Winslade removes him from Third Unit and assigns him to administrative work under Primus Collins, while the Saurian operative becomes his official observer. The expedition combines Legion Varus with Saurian, Rigelian, ape, and dogman forces. Because crystal gravity weapons become more destructive around dense metal, the troops must prepare to fight with little armor. Complaints about the observer lead Winslade to return McGill to Third Unit, but he imposes a King of the Hill exercise as punishment. McGill's unit must defend the central hill against every other unit in its cohort using primitive weapons. Through camouflage, misdirection, careful use of wounded defenders, and repeated counterattacks, Third Unit defeats several larger formations. Sargon dominates the long-range fighting and is fatally wounded during the final assault, while McGill breaks the attackers' center. Third Unit still holds the hill when time expires. Graves briefly makes Leeson acting centurion, then secures McGill's return to combat command before the expedition reaches its target.

A stealthy crystal fleet approaches, and an allied admiral intercepts Scorpio to incorporate the expedition into a larger defense. Human troops are teleported near enemy vessels with antimatter bombs because ordinary remote weapons cannot survive the enemy's electronic defenses. McGill manually detonates a bomb and dies, then revives aboard Scorpio. The bombing waves cripple much of the crystal fleet, allowing the allied ships to close range and destroy the remainder. Crystal World's ground batteries still prevent a safe approach. During a tense command conference, the admiral proposes sacrificing allied ships, nearly breaking the coalition. Winslade preserves cooperation and asks McGill for another plan. McGill suggests a close hyperspace jump followed by immediate bombardment and deployment. The commanders accept the high-risk concept for technical refinement. At a later banquet, Primus Collins is assigned to monitor McGill. She makes clear that their former personal relationship does not excuse informal treatment in public. An investigation concerning McGill also remains active.

McGill learns from an expendable alien pilot, whom he nicknames Seven, that the invasion will use a fragile assault capsule instead of a conventional fleet approach. Third Unit must teleport down first with limited metal equipment and establish the beachhead. McGill gives Seven his own escape harness before the capsule jumps. The unit lands on a breathable but sulfurous Crystal World, activates gateway posts, and discovers settlements inhabited by shape-changing rock bodies. The capsule is destroyed, scout Cooper disappears, and the settlements empty. Saurian troops begin deploying, but the inhabitants attack and tunnel beneath the defenses. They destroy a gateway post and kill Kivi while she works on it. Carlos captures a living fragment, and Natasha suggests that each apparent creature may be a silicon-based colony. Evelyn Thompson is called to study it. Claver X arrives with ape and dogman troops as a far larger northern settlement empties. During a night assault, silicoids destroy both gateway sites, isolate the beachhead, and demonstrate deliberate planning. The coalition retakes the hilltop but expects a larger attack before dawn.

Replacement gateway posts restore the beachhead before a coordinated silicoid offensive. Claver X's forces destroy crystalline drones at extreme cost, while a larger underground attack breaks the Saurian line. McGill brings fresh Legion Varus troops to the hilltop and helps preserve the gateways. The Saurian survivors accuse Legion Varus of withholding troops. As Winslade and other Varus officers arrive, a landmine kills Winslade and wounds Cherish Collins. Graves determines that Varus did not plant it. The Saurian tribune, Claver X, and Galina's father's operative admit arranging Winslade's death because they considered him unfit to lead. Rather than remain exposed to further tunneling attacks, the coalition marches toward the enormous red launcher. The operative suggests that water can kill the low-moisture silicoids, and Evelyn Thompson confirms the idea with a captive. Graves reroutes the force between lakes for protection. Winslade revives, returns, and resumes command. At the launcher, McGill proposes attacking its internal controls. Winslade assigns him a one-way commando insertion with Harris, Natasha, Carlos, Sargon, and other troops.

McGill's commandos teleport to the launcher with no return charge. Natasha identifies their explosives as EMP devices meant to suppress defenses rather than destroy the structure. After deploying them, the team loses communications and climbs an external stairway while the launcher rotates, throwing several soldiers to their deaths. The survivors enter an exhaust channel as coalition reinforcements land and battle silicoids around the weapon. When communications return, Graves warns that the launcher is aligned with Earth and orders McGill to stop it despite instructions to capture the technology intact. Natasha devises a plan to obstruct multiple exhaust ports, while McGill throws plasma grenades into the firing system. The launcher explodes before it can strike Earth. The blast kills the entire commando team and every coalition fighter nearby. Revived on Earth, McGill attends Graves's judgment. Wurtenberger, now consul, holds Graves responsible, demotes him, orders his execution, and sentences him to confinement before possible restored service. Winslade disavows the order, leaving McGill uncertain about the true command chain.

McGill returns to Earth after roughly four months away while many Legion Varus soldiers still await revival. Wurtenberger has taken the consulship during Galina's absence. Seven, restored through human revival technology, accepts an Earth contract as an adviser on the fragmented Galactic powers. Alexander Turov acknowledges that he ordered McGill to damage the coalition, but not to destroy the captured launcher. He suspends McGill's punishment while emphasizing that Earth lost a defensive system it cannot reproduce. McGill finally travels to Dust World, where unusual plants and illicit trade surround the expanded hidden revival operation. Boudica takes him to the newly revived Galina and orders both of them to leave. After McGill brings Galina to her Central City home, Galina tells him that Boudica had her killed twice during captivity. She learns that Wurtenberger became consul and prepares to defend her imperator position after her long absence. McGill returns to his family and discovers that Etta and Derek have married. After initial anger, he accepts Derek as family.

characters.description: A farmer, Candle Scholar Tower mage, and leader of the Eternal Flame. He returns from the Millennium Meeting as a recognized dragon slayer and rejects the Resplendent Empress's attempt to make peace.
characters.name: John

characters.description: John's wife and partner, a powerful mage who ascended alongside him during the Millennium Meeting. She returns at his side and briefly falls under the Resplendent Empress's glamour before John frees her.
characters.name: Ellie

characters.description: The world spirit who administers and defends the Valley. She oversees its quest and resurrection systems and directs exploration.
characters.name: Rabia

characters.description: John's bull companion and a formidable ally. Alongside John and Ellie, he helped stop the hostile coalition from claiming the war god's domain during the Millennium Meeting.
characters.name: Ferdie

characters.description: John's former mentor and a trusted farmhand. John releases him from hired work and offers him land in the Valley, giving Thomas the opportunity to establish a farm and home of his own.
characters.name: Thomas

characters.description: A puppet guide who escorts John and Ellie to the Millennium Meeting prize room. The guide explains their resource worlds, library token, and challenger qualification.
characters.name: the Millennium Meeting puppet guide

characters.description: A self-aware puppet guide associated with Millennium City. Already known to John and Ellie from an earlier visit, he receives them when they return using Ellie's platinum library token.
characters.name: Kevin

characters.description: Ferdie's partner, who is pregnant when John gathers the Valley's allies for the coming war. She stands with Ferdie as the beast forces prepare to support the campaign.
characters.name: the Beast King

characters.description: The true-dragon ruler of the Resplendent Empire and sister of a dragon John previously killed. She approaches him with an offer of peace, but he rejects the proposal and confirms that their war will continue.
characters.name: the Resplendent Empress

characters.description: A powerful dragonkin forge authority in Elmra and the forge overseer's daughter. She takes charge of John's slave group for dangerous blade experiments that appear to consume prisoners.
characters.name: the female dragonkin

characters.description: A human bodyguard serving an influential dragonkin woman in Elmra. Though he protects her publicly, he quietly saves prisoners from her dangerous experiments and directs the survivors into forge labor.
characters.name: the female dragonkin's bodyguard

characters.description: A guard captain who survives John's attempt to free him from draconic corruption. He conceals the portal incident, escorts John to Port Clay, and becomes a local aide in the infiltration.
characters.name: the freed Persis guard captain

characters.description: The Port Clay official who survives purification and willingly joins John to seek revenge against the Empire for his family's destruction. John appoints him acting slave master and places the city's slave operation under his control.
characters.name: the Port Clay vice slave master

characters.description: The ruler of Elmra's forge system and father of an ambitious dragonkin smith. He mistakes John for a returning rival dragon, reveals his descent from that dragon's surviving bloodline, and agrees to help organize a coup.
characters.name: the Elmra forge overseer

characters.description: A senior Imperial investigator dispatched to Elmra after its expanding legion attracts suspicion. He leads an inspection of the forge overseer's activities and represents a serious threat to the concealed uprising.
characters.name: the High Inquisitor

characters.description: The forge overseer's dragonkin daughter, driven by a determination to become a capable blacksmith. She knowingly accepts a potentially fatal Eternal Flame transformation for the chance to advance her craft.
characters.name: Lucia

characters.description: A former enemy-team leader who has become a devil and leads an Abyssal force into Resplendent under the Empress's pact. He invokes a greater power through a blood covenant and demands John's destruction.
characters.name: the enemy elven supreme mage

characters.description: A returning allied spellcaster whom John appoints as his representative to organize Resplendent alongside Rabia after the world joins his divine kingdom.
characters.name: John's Resplendent representative

characters.description: A dragonkin ally appointed to govern Elmra and the former Resplendent Empire. As emperor of the renamed Eternal Empire, he administers its worlds with a dragonkin council.
characters.name: the Eternal Empire emperor

characters.description: The head librarian's husband and John and Ellie's guide through Millennium City. He describes the titan-built city, its library and research districts, and the long cycle governing the Magical Millennium Meeting.
characters.name: the Millennium City guide

characters.description: The head librarian of Millennium City and the guide's wife. She confirms that both she and her husband came from Earth long ago and invites John and Ellie to seek answers about titan creations and their old world.
characters.name: Mina

characters.description: John's younger brother and his closest family connection on Earth. He runs the family cheese shop with his wife Sarah and their daughter Nora, and has lived with an official explanation for John's disappearance.
characters.name: Isaac

characters.description: The authority responsible for Earth's protection and for maintaining magic, faith miracles, and the Endless Worlds. The Administrator permits John and Ellie one tightly limited Earth visit in return for a future service.
characters.name: the Prime Administrator

characters.description: A fundamental law bonded to the Millennium City guide, who serves as its anchor. It explains that personal ties help aspects preserve their identities. Its authority can rewrite reality by revising the past itself.
characters.name: the truth aspect

characters.description: A deity with knowledge of aspects and the powers operating beyond ordinary worlds. The raven god explains how the Eternal Flame could let its bearer consume divinities and eventually embody a fundamental law.
characters.name: the raven god

characters.description: A guide who accompanies John and Ellie into the battlefield. He explains the danger posed by the Unmaking, including crystal entities capable of inhabiting dead dragon bodies and resisting ordinary attacks.
characters.name: the raven god's associate

characters.description: An aspect-powered fighter who intervenes at the battlefield's final wall against a dragon corpse overrun by hostile crystal.
characters.name: the aspect of change avatar

characters.description: A tower keeper who had custody of an Unmaking corpse. John finds hidden crystal threaded through her body and tower, with the growth influencing her mind as the wider site is placed under lockdown.
characters.name: the Candle Scholar Tower master

recaps.ending:
John eradicates the Unmaking outbreak at Candle Scholar Tower and emerges as the holder of the linked aspects Life and Death. The change is immediately dangerous: souls cease to fade and new life stops beginning. With the raven god's help, John restores conception and permits the accumulated dead to pass into true death, declining to establish reincarnation. Ellie remains his central anchor as he struggles to keep the laws from overwhelming his individual identity.

John gives up direct command of the Eternal Flame's expanding exploration effort and leaves its divisions under a council. Rabia continues to administer the enlarged divine kingdom and the Eternal Empire. Thomas establishes his own farm and marries, while Ferdie and his wife have a daughter. John seals Sutton Farm away and spends the winter grounding himself through ordinary work and observation. By spring he is steadier, though still unable to treat his authority casually. The aspect of change avatar then brings evidence that a cult deity may be a hidden dragon. John joins the investigation with the avatar and the raven god's associate, expecting to return home to Ellie after the hunt.
recaps.in_short: After winning the Millennium Meeting, John turns his power against the Resplendent Empire. He infiltrates its slave system, builds a hidden Eternal Flame network, recruits dragonkin dissidents, and creates a ten-thousand-soldier legion. The invasion ends with the dragon Empress's consciousness destroyed and her soul remnants trapped in John's shadow. Rabia takes authority over the conquered worlds, which join John's divine kingdom as the Eternal Empire. John resigns from Candle Scholar Tower, visits Earth, and learns that his altered soul contains two incomplete dragons and can sustain aspects. When Unmaking crystal infects Candle Scholar Tower, he destroys the infestation and becomes the dual aspect Life and Death. His new authority disrupts both conception and the passage of souls until he corrects it. He retreats to Sutton Farm with Ellie to preserve his identity, but leaves in spring to investigate signs of another possible dragon.

recaps.text:
Previously: John is a farmer, powerful mage, Candle Scholar Tower Master, and bearer of the Eternal Flame. Ellie is his wife and partner, with formidable storm magic of her own. Their allies include Rabia, the world spirit who administers the Valley, and Ferdie, John's bull companion and a leader among its beasts. The Valley has become John's divine kingdom, linking his authority to its people and systems.

John has already killed a dragon and retains power connected to that victory. The dead dragon's sister rules the Resplendent Empire, a multiworld power that uses draconic influence to control its subjects. John and the Empress are enemies. He has also survived the Magical Millennium Meeting, where the Candle Scholar Tower team confronted hostile factions and the threat of a devil incursion. As the final results approach, John wants to protect Ellie, his friends, and the Valley without returning to the ruthless identity shaped by his earlier war. His long-term hope remains a quiet life on the farm, but the conflict with the Resplendent Empire stands between him and that retirement.

John, Ellie, and the Candle Scholar Tower team return from the Millennium Meeting. The dragon Empress offers peace, but John sees that her soul is failing and rejects her. Candle Scholar Tower is declared the winner, receiving resource worlds, premier library access, ancient ruin coordinates, and a qualification that could let John pursue power beyond the tenth rank. He refuses the one-way opportunity because Ellie could not accompany him.

Back at Candle Scholar Tower, the Empire's pressure is driving away trade and students. John gives the resource worlds to the tower, retains several artifacts, and closes most outside access while he prepares a response. In the Valley, Rabia reports that resurrection, exploration, settlement, and void travel are all expanding. John tells Ellie that he believes only he can stop the Empress, while promising himself he will not become the person he was during his previous war.

The Valley's leaders pledge themselves to a campaign aimed at dismantling the Empire rather than destroying its worlds. John assigns Rabia's mages and adventurers, Ferdie's beast forces, and allied fighters distinct battlefield roles. His first move will be a solo infiltration to test whether the Eternal Flame can remove draconic control and create an opening for the army.

John studies the Resplendent Empire as a dragon-controlled caste state whose subjects are bound through chains of draconic authority. He decides that the best disguise is to appear to be another dragon. After securing funds and intelligence in the Void Market, he arranges illegal passage to Persis. The smugglers betray him to Imperial guards, but he defeats them and begins testing the Eternal Flame against their corruption.

Several early attempts kill guards whose souls are too deeply damaged. John eventually learns to match the flame to each subject's strength, freeing a captain and three guards. The survivors retain a flame that imitates his apparent draconic aura, allowing them to pass as loyal Imperial servants. From them he learns how Persis imports slaves and gradually converts them into adherents.

In Port Clay, John targets the machinery of that system. He places protective sparks in incoming slaves, removes the slave master, and converts the vice slave master and palace guard captain into allies. The former vice slave master takes control of the operation, while John replaces the city's health inspectors and brings mandatory screening under his influence. Port Clay's enormous slave intake now quietly spreads protection from draconic corruption, giving John a concealed network inside the Empire.

John enters Elmra disguised as a slave and is assigned to its forge system. He discovers a world where accelerated mana production consumes workers and materials alike. Lucia's guard quietly spares him from her dangerous blade experiments, and John's exceptional smithing brings him before her father, the forge overseer. The overseer mistakes John for the return of a rival dragon and reveals that his family belongs to that dragon's surviving bloodline. John recruits him to build an internal coup.

Port Clay begins sending protected slaves to Elmra, where they form a concealed legion. Imperial scrutiny follows. John avoids exposing the plot, uses the Eternal Flame to strengthen the city's smiths, and begins guiding Lucia's efforts to become a blacksmith. She accepts a dangerous transformation that combines Eternal Flame with the dragon power in John's shadow. She survives with a mixed soul flame that can redirect other dragonkin without the agony of direct purification. Her guard accepts John's war blessing and grows stronger.

Lucia's presence begins changing the visiting investigators. When a resistant Inquisitor attacks, John kills him and reveals himself to the two survivors. The High Inquisitor and his subordinate accept the mixed flame and help conceal the death. By the end of the preparations, the ten-thousand-soldier slave legion is armed, faith-linked, and ordered into the first wave bound for Resplendent.

The slave legion enters Resplendent with John and the forge overseer. John records the world's coordinates, leaves the legion under Lucia's guard, and confronts the Empress in her capital. His attack reveals that she is also Resplendent's world spirit, making a careless victory dangerous to the world itself. Ellie, Rabia, Ferdie, allied beasts, and adventurer teams arrive through a distributed portal network and engage the Imperial army.

The Empress invokes an Abyssal pact, but the greater devils refuse to fight John. The enemy elven supreme mage calls on an ancient god, which also declines to oppose John and abandons the mage. John destroys the mage's body and devil soul permanently. He then takes the Empress into the void, destroys her body, and traps her surviving dragon soul beside her brother's remnant in his shadow. The Eternal Flame shatters her consciousness while leaving the immortal remnants bound.

John transfers Resplendent's world authority to Rabia. He offers the dragonkin a final choice under a world-spanning cleansing flame, and those who accept survive free of the Empress's corruption. Elmra and Persis are purified as well. All three worlds join John's divine kingdom as the Eternal Empire. John abolishes slavery and the caste system, appoints a new emperor and council, and leaves Rabia to help administer the transition.

With the war over, John gives Thomas land for an independent farm and resigns from Candle Scholar Tower so his conflicts with higher powers will not endanger it. He and Ellie travel through the Divine Market and then return to Millennium City, where Kevin receives them and the head librarian's husband becomes their guide. Mina, the head librarian, confirms that she and her husband originated on Earth.

The Prime Administrator grants John and Ellie a brief Earth visit in exchange for an unspecified future service. John reunites with his brother Isaac and learns that his family is safe, but his divine presence destabilizes Earth and forces an early departure. Mina later explains that Earth is a real soul-level construct. She also finds two incomplete dragon souls within John's shadow and concludes that his dragon-altered soul can contain powers ordinary people cannot.

John and Ellie learn that ancient gods embody portions of fundamental laws. At the Temple of Ancient Gods, the gate pressure completes Ellie's transformation into lightning and she qualifies as a low ancient god. John breaks through with far greater speed, though combining his domains strains his control. Their guide reveals that he anchors an aspect of truth and explains that anchors preserve an aspect's identity. John and Ellie leave their costly registration decision unresolved.

The raven god explains that the Eternal Flame can anchor its bearer through many believers and may allow John to consume divinities until he becomes an aspect. John and Ellie accompany the raven god's associate into the battlefield, where defenders contain the Unmaking behind a series of walls. The Unmaking are parasitic crystal entities capable of occupying dead dragon bodies. An avatar empowered by the aspect of change destroys one such body.

The group realizes that a stored Unmaking corpse at Candle Scholar Tower may have been exposed to mana, which causes the crystal to multiply rapidly. During an assault on the battlefield, John opens a portal, destroys a vast concentration of crystal, and returns with Ellie and the associate. They find a tower master and three assistants infected, with the structure itself compromised.

John evacuates the uninfected occupants, removes the entire tower into the void, and confronts a developing nest below it. By studying the crystal's linked destruction and regrowth, he recognizes his own domains as the paired aspect Life and Death. He extinguishes the infestation's life force, restores the infected people, repairs the tower, and returns it. The outbreak is ended, but John has become the holder of two fundamental laws.

John returns to the Valley with Ellie and tries to ground himself in farm work. His two trapped dragon souls allow him to sustain Life and Death together, while Ellie helps keep the laws from replacing his personal identity. He helps Thomas establish a farm and home. Thomas marries his partner, and Ferdie and his wife welcome a daughter.

As the Eternal Flame's explorers reach inhabited worlds, casualties and diplomatic conflicts increase. John authorizes an Order divided among explorers, Lore Keepers, and knights, with Rabia implementing the system. He then discovers that souls have accumulated under his authority on an immense scale. The raven god helps him understand that his linked aspects have stopped both the fading of souls and the beginning of new life. John restarts conception, permits the dead to pass into the void, and declines to create reincarnation.

John withdraws from direct command, places the Order under civilian leadership, seals the Valley from outsiders, and hides Sutton Farm while he learns restraint. Ellie and ordinary farm life remain his anchors through the winter. By spring he is steadier and working the land again. The aspect of change avatar brings evidence of a cult deity that may be a hidden dragon. John joins the avatar and the raven god's associate to investigate, intending to return home for dinner.
